definitions.explanation: Creating a copy that imitates the appearance of a genuine article. Often carries a negative connotation when referring to counterfeit goods, but can be neutral when referring to reproductions or replicas.

examples.japanese: {模造|もぞう}{品|ひん}に{注意|ちゅうい}してください。
この{宝石|ほうせき}は{模造|もぞう}ダイヤだった。
examples.english: This gem turned out to be an imitation diamond.

examples.japanese: {有名|ゆうめい}ブランドの{模造|もぞう}{品|ひん}を{販売|はんばい}することは{法律|ほうりつ}で{禁止|きんし}されている。
examples.english: Selling counterfeit products of famous brands is prohibited by law.

notes: Common collocations: {模造|もぞう}{品|ひん} (counterfeit product, imitation), {模造|もぞう}{刀|とう} (imitation sword, replica sword), {模造|もぞう}{紙|し} (poster paper — a specific type of large-format paper, despite the name). {模造|もぞう}{紙|し} is a notable exception where the word does not imply counterfeit but refers to a specific product. Related: {偽物|にせもの} (fake), {レプリカ} (replica), {本物|ほんもの} (genuine article).
